official.deadline_note: No separate scholarship deadline exists. The scholarship is only awarded to eligible applicants within the Master's Main Admission round: application period 7-21 January 2027 (closes 15:00 UTC+2), attachments due 28 January 2027 at 15:00 (UTC+2), results and any scholarship decision by 31 May 2027 at the latest. Hanken states the scholarship decision is given simultaneously with the admission decision and, under the Universities Act, scholarship decisions cannot be appealed.

official.tuition_coverage_note: The GBSN Honor scholarship includes a full tuition fee waiver for two academic years (equivalent to 15 000 EUR/year; Hanken's Master's tuition fee is 15 000 euro/academic year). The tuition fee covers educational expenses such as courses, academic supervision, exams, counselling and university support services; the tuition fee does not cover living costs, personal study related costs such as study materials, or other costs charged under university rules or national legislation, and it does not cover the compulsory Student Union membership fee or the Student Health Care fee.

applicant_utility.summary: This is the only scholarship Hanken awards at admission, it covers tuition completely for two years, and only two people win it - but you never apply for it separately. You simply tick the GBSN Honor Scholarship on the Hanken admission form in the 7-21 January 2027 Main Admission round, and the decision arrives with your admission result. Confirm on the GBSN membership page that your school is a current member and in one of the 21 listed countries before you spend money on GMAT/GRE and language tests. Budget for everything except tuition: living costs in Helsinki run roughly 950-1200 EUR per month, and Finnish migration rules require proof of about 9 600 EUR per year before a residence permit is granted.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Degree students or recent graduates of GBSN member business schools in the 21 listed developing countries who are tuition-liable and can meet the January Main Admission deadline with a strong academic file.
application_readiness_checklist: Verify your institution is a current GBSN member school located in one of the 21 eligible countries (GBSN membership page) before applying
Book GMAT/GRE/IELTS/TOEFL early - results must be valid through the application period, and TOEFL scores must be sent to Hanken under reporting code 8433
Prepare the English CV and degree transcripts as high-quality PDFs before opening the Studyinfo.fi form, because it cannot be saved as a draft
Complete and upload every attachment by 28 January 2027 at 15:00 (UTC+2) - late uploads stop the application from being processed
Pay the 100 EUR application fee if you are from a non-EU/EEA country
Use an email address you will still access until at least September 2027, since scholarship and admission news arrive there
common_rejection_risks: Applying in the Rolling Admission round or after 21 January 2027 - the scholarship is only available in the Main Admission round
Forgetting to tick the GBSN Honor Scholarship box on the admission form, since there is no separate application and no later correction
Assuming any business school in a listed country qualifies - the school itself must be a GBSN member
Missing the 28 January attachment deadline or uploading a school certificate that does not clearly state English as the language of tuition
Being tuition-exempt (EU/EEA citizen or qualifying Finnish permit), which makes you ineligible because the waiver only applies to tuition-liable students
Falling below the 3.00 minimum academic assessment score or the 25-30 ECTS relevant-studies threshold
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Living costs (about 950-1200 EUR/month in Helsinki, 800-1000 in Vaasa), the 100 EUR application fee, aptitude and language test fees (roughly 100-300 EUR and 200-450 EUR), residence permit fee 400-750 EUR, health insurance about 450 EUR, Student Union membership 70 EUR/year and the student health care fee 70.70 EUR/academic year - the scholarship waives tuition only.
document_audit: The Studyinfo.fi form cannot be saved as a draft; answers determine which attachments are requested and cannot be changed after submission
If claiming English proficiency from a prior degree, the language of tuition must be explicitly stated on an official certificate, transcript or diploma supplement
TOEFL must be sent via reporting code 8433; IELTS One Skill Retake and TOEFL MyBest scores are not accepted
If exempt from tuition fees by residence permit, upload both sides of the permit card with the application
alerts: Only 2 scholarships exist per year across all eligible countries, so treat this as a long shot alongside other funding
You cannot change study location (Helsinki/Vaasa) or programme after accepting the offer
Scholarship decisions cannot be appealed under the Universities Act, and the 25% Early Commitment discount is not available to scholarship recipients
Second-year continuation requires 60 completed ECTS and a 3.0 GPA by 31 July each year, plus a commitment to limited student recruitment activities
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Fill in the joint Studyinfo.fi application between 7-21 January 2027 with the GBSN Honor Scholarship ticked, pay the application fee, upload attachments by 28 January, then wait for the combined admission and scholarship e-mail with results by 31 May 2027 at the latest.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a one-time recognition grant of up to 7 500 euros for late-stage ICT doctoral researchers, paid straight to you in December - it will not cover tuition or rent, so treat it as a career-building award rather than funding. The right moment to apply is when you already have one or more accepted publications destined for your dissertation. Your principal supervisor must be a professor, docent, or senior scientist at your university and must personally submit the commitment statement through the electronic tool, so agree the timing with them well before the mid-September deadline. You can only ever receive this scholarship once, and Finnish applicants doing their doctorate abroad can apply too.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Advanced doctoral researchers in ICT or ICT-enabling fields at Finnish universities (and Finnish nationals abroad) who have accepted dissertation publications and a supervisor senior enough to vouch for them.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you have at least one accepted publication intended for the dissertation before drafting the application
Check that your principal supervisor holds a professor, docent, or senior scientist position at your university
Agree with your supervisor early that they will enter the commitment statement in the electronic application tool themselves
Prepare the application in the Foundation's system at nokiafoundation.apurahat.net as soon as the window opens in early August
Watch nokiafoundation.com in December for the recipient announcement and payment
common_rejection_risks: Applying too early, before any accepted publication exists - the Foundation explicitly frames the optimal time as having accepted dissertation publications
Supervisor not meeting the professor/docent/senior-scientist bar, or failing to submit the commitment statement through the tool
Pursuing a doctorate too distant from ICT or ICT-supporting fields to qualify
Assuming the award can be received twice - it is granted only once per individual
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Everything except the grant itself: the scholarship is a one-off payment to the researcher and does not pay tuition, living costs, conference travel, or research expenses.
document_audit: The commitment statement is entered by the supervisor in the electronic tool - do not assume you can upload it on their behalf
Publications must be accepted and intended for inclusion in the dissertation, not merely submitted or in preparation
alerts: The window is short - about six weeks from early August to the 15 September deadline
If you have already received a Nokia Scholarship you cannot apply again
The Foundation publishes recipients only in December, so plan any spending around a late-December payment
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: You file the application in the electronic grant system during the August-September window, your supervisor submits the commitment statement in the same system, and awards are announced and paid in December.
